stem: While compiling waitlist education for a solid-organ candidate, which community provider relationship should the coordinator ensure is in place per standard references?

options.text: A primary care provider to assist with health maintenance and acute health needs in addition to the transplant team
Only the transplant surgeon with no primary care involvement
A cosmetic specialist as the sole ongoing medical contact
No community providers because all care must remain hospital-based forever

explanation.rationale_correct: In addition to the transplant team, patients should have a primary care provider to attend to and assist with their health maintenance and acute health needs while awaiting and after transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Transplant care is coordinated with a primary care provider rather than excluding community medical support.
rationale_incorrect.C: Health maintenance and acute needs are addressed through primary care, not cosmetic specialty alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Long-term care includes community primary care alongside the transplant program.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → waitlist responsibilities → iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: patients should have a primary care provider to attend to and assist with their health maintenance and acute health needs

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → waitlist patient responsibilities → iv. (primary care provider for health maintenance and acute needs); PDF p. 102 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Ninth 020200 item; PCP coordination angle distinct from skin/dentition screening (cctc-2051) and bronchoscopy (cctc-2043); anchor verified on Cupples p. 102.

stem: A waitlisted candidate misses organ-specific laboratory testing required to remain active on the list. What waitlist consequence aligns with standard coordinator references?

options.text: Failure to complete required testing may change the candidate's priority on the waitlist
Missing required testing automatically grants higher waitlist priority
Required testing applies only after transplantation, not while waitlisted
Waitlist priority is unaffected by completion of required studies

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidates must obtain required diagnostic studies while waiting to remain viable and active on the list; failure to complete required testing may result in a change in the candidate's priority on the waitlist.

rationale_incorrect.B: Missing required testing may lower or alter priority rather than automatically increasing it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Organ-specific labs such as those supporting LAS or MELD may be required while waitlisted to remain active.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist priority can change when required testing is not completed.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → waitlist responsibilities → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Failure to complete required testing may result in a change in candidate's priority on the waitlist

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → waitlist responsibilities → ii. (required studies to remain active; failure may change waitlist priority); PDF p. 102 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Ninth 020500 item; required-testing priority angle distinct from OPTN removal (cctc-2049) and inactive accrual (cctc-2037); anchor verified on Cupples p. 102.

stem: A candidate's waitlist status changes after updated testing. What communication responsibility aligns with standard coordinator references?

options.text: Educate the candidate about the waitlist status change and rationale for additional tests or procedures
Withhold all waitlist updates until the candidate discovers changes independently
Communicate changes only to the insurance company, not the candidate
Defer all waitlist communication until after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Transplant coordinator waitlist responsibilities include educating candidates about any changes in their waitlist status and the rationale for additional tests or procedures.

rationale_incorrect.B: Candidates should be educated about waitlist status changes rather than left to discover them without explanation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Waitlist education is directed to the candidate as part of coordinator communication responsibilities.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist communication occurs during the waiting period, not deferred until after transplant.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → coordinator responsibilities → iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Educate candidates about any changes in their waitlist status and rationale for additional tests or procedures

stem: An adolescent solid-organ recipient is preparing to transfer from the pediatric to the adult transplant program. Which coordinator role aligns with standard transition references?

options.text: Pediatric and adult transplant coordinators facilitate education and communication during the vulnerable transition period
Transition requires no coordinator involvement once the patient turns 18
Only the pediatric coordinator remains responsible indefinitely with no adult program contact
Transition means the recipient stops all transplant follow-up permanently

explanation.rationale_correct: Transition from pediatric to adult care is a vulnerable period, and pediatric and adult transplant coordinators play a critical role through individual patient education and communication between programs.

rationale_incorrect.B: Coordinators on both sides support the transition rather than ending involvement at a birthday alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Adult program coordinators share responsibility during transition rather than pediatric coordinators retaining sole indefinite responsibility.
rationale_incorrect.D: Transition transfers ongoing transplant care to the adult program rather than ending follow-up.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 17, Pediatric Populations → H. Transition from pediatric to adult care → 2.
